Thanks for the note, Danielle — good question. Short answer: for Acme (controller) -> Redwood (processor) the appropriate path is Module 2 (Controller-to-Processor). Module 3 (Processor-to-Processor) is what governs downstream processor relationships (i.e. Redwood -> cloud provider / subprocessors).

I'm looping in Laura Bennett (Legal) and Priyom Das (Privacy Ops) to provide the exact language we prefer and to attach a draft SCC and security annex. We are generally agreeable to the EU SCCs + UK Addendum where applicable and will propose minimal, implementation-focused redlines rather than doctrinal changes.

I'll attach a draft for review in a follow-up.

Hi Danielle and team,

Apologies for the delayed reply — thanks for raising these items. From a contractual perspective:

1) Module selection
- Acme -> Redwood: Module 2 (Controller -> Processor) is the correct module.
- Redwood -> any subprocessors (cloud infra, analytics vendors): Module 3 will apply in those downstream agreements. We typically accept Module 3 language in our subprocessors' flow-downs.

2) UK Addendum
- We execute the EU Commission SCCs as the primary instrument and then attach the UK Addendum (where the transfer involves UK entities or UK nationals). For clarity, we can provide a single docset: EU SCCs + UK Addendum (combined package) for signing. That is our standard approach.

3) Annexes (I/II/III) & redlines
- Annex I (description of processing): please confirm the categories you consider "special category" / health data — we recommend conservative categorizations to avoid later disputes.
- Annex II (technical & organizational measures): we will propose Redwood's baseline measures (encryption in transit & at rest, role-based access, logging, incident response SLA). See attached "Redwood-Technical-Security-Annex.pdf" for our standard text. We request any additional controls you require be documented now.
- Annex III (subprocessor list): we will provide an up-to-date subprocessors list and commit to notice for additions.

4) HIPAA / US-specific considerations
- If Acme requires a HIPAA-compliant BAA for US patient data, please flag that explicitly. Redwood can discuss a BAA or equivalent contractual commitment for covered activities; operational model matters (hosted vs private) will affect scope.

Next steps: I attached a draft "Redwood_SCC_Draft_Module2_v1.docx" reflecting Module 2 + UK addendum language and a data flow diagram that Priyom prepared. If you like, we can agree redlines and we will route a DocuSign packet for signature.

Regards,

Redwood Inference
